title: The 100 billion dollar race to build humanoid robots

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: What will a 100 billion dollar investment in humanoid robots mean for our future — and who will benefit most?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Current tech can build basic bipedal robots, but dexterous manipulation and real-time learning remain major hurdles.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: If robots replace human labor, we risk deepening inequality and eroding the value of human work and creativity.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Builders are focusing on collaborative robots that enhance, not replace, human capabilities in manufacturing and healthcare.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: Imagine robots aiding the elderly or disabled, freeing humans to pursue art, education, and community-building.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The race ahead will define whether robots uplift or displace — the outcome depends on choices made today.

video_cue: A humanoid robot assisting an elderly person in a modern home, with holographic data overlays showing real-time health monitoring.
